votes.evidence:
Premise confirmed by tracing the flag from producer to consumer in /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215:

1. Flag is team-wide, no repository parameter: products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config(team_id)` is `.for_team(team_id).filter(enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False).exclude(installation_id="").exists()`. products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:72-81 returns it as `stamphog_connected`.

2. Actual gate is per PR repository, silent on miss: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1137-1152 resolves `StamphogRepoConfig ... .filter(provider="github", repository__iexact=repository, enabled=True, ...)` and on `None` does `logger.info("stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable", ...)` and `return`. No run row, no PR comment, nothing reaches the UI.

3. The trigger is the product's own default, not an edge case: products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:302-316 binds EVERY repo in the installation with `defaults={"team_id": ..., "enabled": False}` and the comment says "connect them but don't start reviewing until a human toggles each on". So a team that enabled repo A and left repo B at its synced-but-disabled default has `stamphog_connected=True`, the toggle on, and inbox PRs against B skipped silently.

4. Copy reads as project-level: settings.py:27-33 toggle help_text "Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository (see stamphog_connected)"; products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1054-1057 row description is unconditional ("When a self-driving implementation from your Inbox opens a pull request, Stamphog reviews it and approves it if it passes"); the disabledReason at 1066-1067 says "Connect a repository to Stamphog first". Only the model docstring (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:277-280, "covering the PR's repository") states the per-repo rule, and users never see it. `stamphog_connected` is the sole conditional input to that row (grep: line 1066 is its only use in the scene).

5. Tests only cover the team-level semantics: products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:60-75 parameterizes on one repo config; nothing exercises the enabled-A/disabled-B case.
votes.refutation:
Attempted refutations:
(a) The `stamphog_connected` help_text (settings.py:50-54) is accurate for what it computes and only makes a claim about the false case ("has nothing to act on"), so the field itself is not wrong. This holds, but it does not cover the toggle's help_text or the UI row description, which are what a user reads and which imply one connected repo is enough.
(b) The flag's only consumer is a disabledReason gate for the "nothing connected at all" state, where it is correct. True, but the finding is about the copy that surrounds the toggle in the connected state, not about the disabled gate.
(c) The skip is logged server-side (tasks.py:1152). It is info-level and internal; no user-facing signal exists, so this only helps an operator, not the user the copy misleads.
(d) Overlap with GB16, which also names the per-repo gap as a secondary point. Overlap does not make it false; both resolve with the same one-sentence copy change.
None of these defeat the core claim. The stronger suggestion in the finding (make the flag per-repository aware from Inbox context) is not warranted, because the settings endpoint has no PR/repo context; the minimal fix is one sentence in the toggle help_text and the UI description saying reviews run only on repositories enabled in Stamphog. Real but minor, so consider.

votes.evidence: Premise verified in the worktree. `has_reviewable_repo_config` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125) is a team-wide `.exists()` over `StamphogRepoConfig` with no repository argument. The real gate in `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1152) filters `repository__iexact=<PR repo>` and returns after only `logger.info("stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable", ...)` when no config covers that repo; the webhook re-review leg does the same per-repo resolve (tasks.py:179-186). The model docstring already states the per-repo rule (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:279-280 "covering the PR's repository"), but the toggle's help_text says "Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository" (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:30-32) and the `stamphog_connected` help_text describes "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository" (settings.py:50-54); the UI disabled message (products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066-1067) reads at project level. Tests confirm the per-repo silent no-op is the intended design, not a bug: `test_inbox_receiver_leg_noops_without_a_reviewable_config` has an explicit `different_repo` case (products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:947-971, comment "Self-scoping (decision): toggle on without a synced+enabled config covering the PR's repository is a silent no-op"). `test_stamphog_connected_requires_a_synced_enabled_repo_config` (products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:60-75) only exercises team-wide semantics. No test, guard, or copy closes the gap between "project has a repository connected" (what the flag and copy say) and "this PR's repository is connected" (what the gate needs). Reachable trigger: a team with repo A synced and Inbox tasks producing PRs against repo B sees the toggle on and enabled, and reviews never run, with no user-visible signal.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) The `stamphog_connected` help_text is literally accurate ("at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository") and never promises reviews for every PR, so the flag itself is not wrong. (2) The disabled-state UI message only fires when nothing is connected at all (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066), which is correct for that state. (3) The silent no-op is a recorded design decision with a dedicated `different_repo` test (test_tasks.py:953, 958-971), and the skip is logged server-side with team and repository, so it is not a behavioral defect. These narrow the finding: the stronger suggestions (per-repo flag from Inbox context, audit event) are out of scope and the diagnostic already exists. What survives is only the toggle help_text at settings.py:30-32 ("when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository"), which contradicts the model docstring's "covering the PR's repository" and can mislead multi-repo teams. That is a real but minor copy-precision issue, not a bug, hence consider rather than should_fix. It also overlaps GB16's second point.

votes.evidence:
Trigger is reachable in production, and it is the default state after connecting, not an edge case:

1. Sync binds every user-accessible repo in the installation but seeds them disabled: `products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:309-316` (`defaults={"team_id": ..., "enabled": False}`, comment: "an installation can surface hundreds of repos, so connect them but don't start reviewing until a human toggles each on"). Webhook-added repos are also created `enabled=False` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:632-636, 665-674`). So a team's normal shape is N synced configs, a subset enabled.

2. `has_reviewable_repo_config` (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:113-125`) is a team-wide `.exists()` over `enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False, installation_id != ""`, no repository argument. One enabled repo flips `stamphog_connected` to true for the whole project.

3. The real gate is per-PR-repository: `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1138-1152` filters `repository__iexact=repository, enabled=True` and on no match logs `stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable` at info level and returns. No run row, no PR comment, no UI signal.

4. Inbox PRs do target multiple repos per team: signals picks the repository per report from a repo-selection artefact (`products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:624-628`) and `SignalsTeamConfig.autostart_base_branches` is a dict keyed by repository (`products/signals/backend/models.py:139`, used at `auto_start.py:518-519`). So "repo A enabled, PR against synced-but-disabled repo B" is an ordinary multi-repo team.

5. Copy: serializer help_text `products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:27-33` ("Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository") and `settings.py:50-54` ("at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository") describe a project-level condition; UI `products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066-1067` says "Connect a repository to Stamphog first", which reads as one connection being sufficient. The model docstring (`products/review_hog/backend/models.py:277-280`) is the only place that says "covering the PR's repository".

Net: the flag/copy imply project-level sufficiency while the effect is per-repository; in the common partially-enabled state a user sees a healthy toggle and gets no review for PRs against a disabled repo.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) The `stamphog_connected` help_text is literally accurate ("at least one synced, enabled repository") and the flag's stated job is only to decide whether the toggle can act at all, so the serializer field itself is not wrong; the mismatch is confined to the toggle help_text and the UI string. (b) Per-repo enablement is a deliberate, product-wide stamphog invariant (webhook reviews also skip disabled repos), and the Stamphog settings expose a per-repo enable list, so a user who enabled only repo A has already made that choice in the product. (c) The skip is not fully silent server-side: `tasks.py:1152` logs team and repository, so operators can diagnose it. (d) Making the flag per-repository would require the settings endpoint to know the Inbox's future target repos, which it cannot; the "stronger fix" in the suggestion is not warranted. None of these make the user-facing copy accurate, so the finding survives as a copy-precision issue only. Severity stays at consider: no incorrect behavior, no data risk, fix is one sentence in help_text and one in the UI string.
